ev_fr_land_cover_fahrudin24_1.quote:
In this study, adjustments were made to the definitions of target 
areas for afforestation and reforestation based on the regulations set by 
the UNFCCC and Ministry of Forestry (MoFE 2015). Afforested areas 
were defined as non-forested regions of > 50 years. However, owing to 
data limitations, an adjusted approach was adopted in which the target 
areas for afforestation were identified by integrating non-forested 
regional information defined as of 2000. This information was sourced 
from Global Forest Watch data (Hansen et al., 2013), integrated with 
impervious surface data from 1983 to 2000 (Gong et al., 2020), and 
MODIS land-cover data since 2000 (USGS, 2010). Consequently, the 
targeted reforestation areas in this study focused on regions with low 
forest cover or non-forested areas observed from 2000 to 2023.

Wide-scale restoration opportunities involve
areas with less intensive land use where a single type of interven-

a population density below 10/km2, and they account for 21 per-
cent of restoration opportunities worldwide (Laestadius et al.
2012). Approaches suitable for wide-scale restoration include
mixed-species plantations or assisted or spontaneous natural rege-
neration. In areas with higher population density (10–100/km2)

thresholds of 10% and 50% in sensitivity analyses

relationship.direction: 30% tree cover separates forest from non-forest (the high end of the UNFCCC 10-30% range), so land below it is the reforestation opportunity space; 10% and 50% alternatives shift the result substantially

tree cover to more than 25% tree cover in areas where forests histori-

relationship.direction: the opportunity space for forest regrowth is land BELOW 25% tree cover that lies where forests historically occurred; restoration is the transition across that 25% threshold

ev_fr_tree_canopy_cover_zomer08_1.quote:

dataset (Hansen et al., 2003), a global dataset of tree canopy
cover extracted from multi-temporal MODIS data (500 m
resolution), was used to identify currently forested areas
within the remaining ‘‘non-forest areas’’. A threshold of
30% canopy cover was used as the forest deﬁnition, as per
results of an earlier analysis of the impact of forest deﬁnition
on areas available at a national scale (Verchot and Zomer,
2007).

ev_market_value_chain_nunes20_1.quote: Estruturar a cadeia produtiva dos produtos de áreas restauradas. Economic use can pay for restoration partially or fully, but the value chain for native timber management and forest products (e.g. non-timber products such as fruits and oils from agroforestry systems) must be strengthened. panels.rules:
Evidence → responses → compatible synthesis → developer table

  1. Read authoritative source and evidence registers. Keep dropped and unresolved records visible in evidence accounting; only eligible reviewed evidence sets compiled responses.
  2. Separate model use, suitability direction and numeric calibration. Species/crop scope, observed site conditions and operational feasibility keep their recorded roles.
  3. Convert units and standardize suitability classes using the versioned policy below. Preserve source ranks, gaps, overlaps and explicit unsuitable classes. Low suitability is not exclusion.
  4. Combine only profiles with approved matching pool, system, context, units and scoring policy. Deduplicate independent origins before weighting. At each interval, take the quality-weighted median; tied median bounds, within-origin conflicts and exclusion disagreements remain unknown.
  5. Rebuild from the full corpus and compare with audited T4. Dataset binding and target transfer are separate decisions. Publish function options and provenance, never an implicit universal choice.

Common class scores loaded from compilation policy

No class-score policy approved for this recipe.

Weights used to combine evidence

Source-quality weight = tier × claim basis × applicable grey-literature discount. These weights reconcile evidence; they are distinct from a variable’s importance in its source model.

Variable importance and spatial MCDA

Source weights are normalized within each complete sibling group, then multiplied along the source hierarchy to obtain whole-model shares. Additive repeat branches are consolidated by variable and scope. Flat ratio = whole-model share × number of distinct variable/scope inputs. Hierarchy-adjusted ratio = whole-model share ÷ equal-share contribution through the same tree. Missing or conflicting models retain holds; these diagnostics do not set runtime weights.

Choose one representative per thematic/correlation group before final weights. Aggregation requires a recipe-specific recorded decision; no method or weight vector is selected by this diagnostic. When a weighted overlay is explicitly selected, weights must sum to one and missing inputs remain unknown, without per-pixel renormalization.

Repairing incomplete curves

Verified continuations of reviewed source tables can be restored under an explicit, content-pinned correction policy. Source pages and agent verification remain visible; human approval flags and reviewed-study counts do not change. This does not create an independent study vote. A highest reported class need not reach 1. Only the recipe-specific class-score policies displayed above may supply scores. Unknown thresholds and contradictory classes remain explicit.

Country and version rules

Target country selects dataset bindings. An optional exact study-country filter narrows evidence and recomputes compatible pools; neither approves transfer. This view uses the full corpus. Published developer bundles are pinned snapshots; this dashboard is the single inspection surface. Review decisions stay in QA/QC.
